text.p: Toro Co, which reported record fiscal 1997 second quarter sales and profits, said it backs analysts estimates for its fiscal 1997 year of $3.10 to $3.20 a share.

"We expect a very challenging second half," said Kendrick Melrose, chairman, in a statement. "While there remains more uncertainty than normal in several of our key market segments, and business has been soft due to the weather, we are comfortable with current market expectations."
Toro, which makes lawn mowers, snow throwers and irrigation equipment, earned $2.90 a share in fiscal 1996.

The company's sales for its fiscal second quarter ended May 2, 1997 rose 22 percent to a record $352.2 million. Net income was $19 million, up 13.1 percent over last year. Earnings per share increased 15 percent to $1.53.
"We are satisfied with our second quarter performance despite a flat sales quarter from our domestic consumer business," Melrose said.
Sales of worldwide consumer business products for the quarter were flat as cool, wet weather reinforced a conservative buying mood among customers, Toro said.

Toro said sales to professional markets, including commercial and irrigation businesses, were strong for the quarter. Commercial equipment sales were up, increasing 12.4 percent over the same period last year.
Sales of equipment to golf courses did well, reflecting the continued growth and popularity of golf as a spectator and player sport, the company said.

Irrigation sales increased 117.9 percent due to the addition of Toro-Hardie irrigation products and an increase in Toro irrigation core products. The integration of Toro-Hardie into Toro is proceeding on track, it added.

International sales increased 27.4 percent due mostly to the addition of Toro-Hardie international sales. Equipment and irrigation sales to the golf market were up as new courses were added in the Philippines, Korea, and Egypt. Golf equipment sales also did well in Europe despite generally weak economic conditions, it said.
Expenses for sales, general, and administrative as a percent of sales were down slightly, reflecting ongoing cost controls, the company said.
Shares of Toro were trading off 1/8 to 37-3/4.
